title: Count Negative Numbers in a Sorted Matrix
prompt: Given an `m x n` matrix `grid` sorted in non-increasing order both row-wise and column-wise (each row and each column is sorted from largest to smallest), return the number of negative numbers in `grid`.
constraints: grid is sorted in non-increasing order row-wise and column-wise
hints: Checking every cell works in O(m*n), but each row being sorted means you can find where negatives start faster than a full scan.
For a fixed row, binary search for the first index where the value becomes negative — everything from there to the end of the row is negative too.

Since columns are also sorted, the boundary between non-negative and negative shifts monotonically as you move down the rows, which lets you reuse work between rows for an O(m log n) or O(m + n) solution.

solution.approach: Each row is sorted in non-increasing order, so within a row all the negative numbers form a contiguous suffix. For each row, binary search for the leftmost index where the value is negative; the count of negatives in that row is n minus that index. Summing this count across all m rows gives the total in O(m log n) time, far better than checking every one of the m*n cells individually.
